name: Sally Lunn (No. 1)
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: ½ teaspoonful soda, dissolved in hot water
ingredients.originalText: ½ teaspoonful soda, dissolved in hot water

instructions.text: Beat the eggs to a stiff froth
Add the milk, water, butter, soda, and salt
Stir in the flour to a smooth batter and beat the yeast in well
Set to rise in a buttered pudding-dish, in which it must be baked and sent to table, or if you wish to turn it out, set to rise in a well-buttered mould
It will not be light under six hours
Bake steadily three-quarters of an hour, or until a straw thrust into it comes up clean

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Beat the eggs to a stiff froth
2. Add the milk, water, butter, soda, and salt
3. Stir in the flour to a smooth batter and beat the yeast in well
4. Set to rise in a buttered pudding-dish, in which it must be baked and sent to table, or if you wish to turn it out, set to rise in a well-buttered mould
5. It will not be light under six hours
6. Bake steadily three-quarters of an hour, or until a straw thrust into it comes up clean
7. Eat while hot
